newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says mega steel contract not terminated.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says mega steel contract not terminated.

text.p: Nigeria's military government said on Monday it had not terminated a contract with Russian firm Tiajpromexport (TPE) for the construction of the $5 billion Ajaokuta steel mill.

"It is not true that the federal government has terminated the Ajaokuta steel project," the power and steel ministry said in a statement in reaction to a recent report by the state news agency that the contract had been ended.
"Rather the present administration is fully committed to the completion of the Ajaokuta steel project during its tenure," it added.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on January 16 quoted sources at the mill as saying TPE had been paid 50 billion naira ($625 million) at the end of 1996 to terminate the contract which is estimated to have cost $5 billion.

The ministry's statement said the government had offset a substantial part of its debt to TPE and a meeting of the two sides was due to be held in Nigeria soon "on possible further relations on Ajaokuta steel project."
Russia began construction of the steel mill in 1979 but Nigeria's failure to pay its debts has stalled completion, which the government says has reached 98 percent.
The Ajaokuta Steel Complex is one of four steel rolling mills ordered by a government awash with oil money in the 1970s, to reduce imports and to use Nigerian iron ore.
The World Bank carried out a study on the complex between 1990 and 1991 and advised government to stop the project, saying it was too capital-intensive.
The present military government says it is committed to completing Ajaokuta.
